excerpt: Decode what US Class A and Class B full-service gross (FSG) office leases actually cover in their Cleaning Specifications Exhibit—and what falls onto your supplemental tenant budget. Price excluded breakrooms, interior conference glass, and quarterly floor care accurately before signing.
quickAnswer: A standard US full service gross (FSG) lease cleaning scope covers 5-night weekday trash removal, horizontal dusting of cleared desks, traffic-lane vacuuming, and core restroom sanitation inside your base rent, while excluding interior breakroom sinks/appliances ($12 to $25/visit), conference glass partitions ($15 to $35/visit), and quarterly deep floor care ($0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month). Supplemental out-of-pocket tenant cleaning add-ons typically total $501 to $1,080 per month for a 5,000 sq ft suite and $1,035 to $2,199 per month for a 15,000 sq ft corporate floor.

blocks.text: Tenants signing a Full-Service Gross (FSG) lease frequently assume "janitorial included" means every surface inside their suite stays spotless at zero extra cost. Two weeks after move-in, complaints start piling up: coffee rings remain on kitchen counters, conference room glass walls show handprints, and private suite showers or executive restrooms go untouched.

The culprit sits in **Exhibit C or D—the Landlord's Cleaning Specifications**. Institutional Class A and Class B landlords write base-building janitorial contracts to protect common assets at minimum cost per square foot, not to deliver hospitality-grade suite upkeep. Understanding exact FSG boundaries—and pricing supplemental add-ons up front—prevents surprise operating expenses during Year 1.
What Standard Full-Service Gross (FSG) Leases Include vs. Exclude

Standard US FSG cleaning exhibits cover **5 nights per week (Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays)** after 6:00 PM. Landlord crews follow strict production routes (often pushing 4,000+ sq ft/hour) focused on core hygiene and basic appearance, leaving specialized suite spaces expressly outside scope.

items: **Included in Base FSG Rent:** Emptying suite wastebaskets (often replacing liners only when soiled), spot-vacuuming open traffic lanes (full wall-to-wall vacuuming is frequently 1x/week), damp-mopping hard entryways, dusting cleared desk tops, and cleaning core multi-tenant restrooms.

**Expressly Excluded From Base FSG Scope:** Sanitizing breakroom sinks, loading dishwashers, cleaning inside microwaves/refrigerators, wiping interior floor-to-ceiling conference glass, cleaning private in-suite executive restrooms, and quarterly carpet extraction or VCT scrub-and-recoat.
**Specialty Hourly Exclusions ($55–$95/hr):** Post-move-in construction dust removal, weekend/holiday shift coverage, high dusting above 8 to 10 feet, and OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens spill remediation.

blocks.title: Beware Base-Year Expense Stops and Gross-Up Clauses
blocks.text: In an FSG lease, base-building cleaning is only fixed during your Base Year. If building occupancy sits at 65% in Year 1, the landlord applies a 95% gross-up clause to normalize variable janitorial expenses—and any wage or union rate increases above your Base Year stop pass through to you as Operating Expense escalations in Years 2 through 10.
Out-of-Pocket Cost of FSG Tenant Supplemental Cleaning Add-Ons

When base-building crews skip your kitchenette and glass conference rooms, tenants either pay the building's master contractor an "above-standard" fee or hire a supplemental vendor (subject to landlord approval). Using US national benchmarks (**$12 to $25/visit** for breakrooms, **$15 to $35/visit** for interior glass, and **$0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month** amortized for quarterly deep floor care) across **13.0 monthly visits** (3x/wk) or **21.65 monthly visits** (5x/wk), here is what FSG add-ons realistically cost.

blocks.text: If your FSG tenant suite also maintains a dedicated reception coffee bar or adds a daytime porter for mid-day catering resets, budget **$35 to $65 per standard labor hour** on top of the add-ons above. Conversely, if you occupy a [triple-net (NNN) lease](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/triple-net-nnn-lease-janitorial-cost-allocation/), you fund the entire base cleaning scope ($0.05 to $0.20/sq ft/visit) directly rather than just supplemental add-ons.
Auditing Landlord Cleaning Exhibits: Common Loopholes & Fixes

Most FSG cleaning disputes happen because lease boilerplate uses vague phrases like "vacuum carpets as needed" or "clean kitchenettes nightly" without defining measurable standards. Compare your landlord's draft exhibit against the common loopholes below before executing a renewal.

rows: Crews only spot-vacuum main aisles; under-desk edges go untouched for weeks
Redline to require full wall-to-wall HEPA vacuuming at least 1x–2x/week and traffic lanes nightly

Explicitly add counter/sink disinfection ($12–$25/visit) or budget a supplemental crew
Covers suite main entry door only; excludes all interior conference room glass walls
Add interior conference partitions ($15–$35/visit) or specify weekly full-pane squeegee service
Applies strictly to multi-tenant core restrooms; private suite restrooms/showers excluded
Verify whether private suite plumbing requires a direct vendor add-on ($15–$30/restroom/visit)
Excludes building holidays and provides no weekend coverage for Saturday teams
Pre-negotiate holiday coverage rates and weekend surcharge rules ($35–$65/hr vs. 1.5x OT)

blocks.text: Hardware Standards for Supplemental FSG Suite Crews

Class A property managers strictly police which contractors enter the building after hours—especially in [multi-floor office buildings](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/multi-floor-office-building-cleaning-cost/) with union labor rules or LEED indoor-air-quality certifications. Any supplemental vendor handling your private breakrooms, medical-grade executive suites, or glass conference rooms must bring quiet, sealed HEPA hardware and splash-controlled wet floor systems that protect neighboring tenants' finishes.

For supplemental suite maintenance, reliable commercial tools include the **Atrix VACBP1 Ergo HEPA Commercial Backpack Vacuum** (8 qt capacity, 99.97% HEPA filtration, 10.3 lb weight, 67 dBA) for fine-particulate carpet care, the **Powr-Flite BP6S Comfort Pro Backpack Vacuum** (6 qt capacity, 5-Stage HEPA filtration, 11 lb chassis, quiet 62 dBA output) for evening suites with late-working staff, and the **Rubbermaid Commercial WaveBrake 35-Quart Mop Bucket & Side-Press Wringer** (35 qt capacity, baffled WaveBrake splash-reduction, side-press wringer rated for 5-year commercial durability) to keep breakroom LVT/VCT floors streak-free without splashing baseboard millwork.

blocks.title: Verify Master Contractor Right-of-First-Refusal Clauses
blocks.text: Many Class A FSG leases forbid outside janitorial vendors inside the tower unless the landlord's master contractor declines the supplemental work or fails to match market pricing. Always confirm COI rules ($1M/$2M GL, Additional Insured, Workers' Compensation) and freight elevator access before bidding out supplemental cleaning.
How to Negotiate FSG Cleaning Scope Before Signing Your Lease

Your greatest leverage over full-service gross cleaning standards happens before lease execution, when a 10-minute redline can lock in $6,000 to $25,000 per year of clear service commitments and keep your [annual office cleaning budget forecast](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/quarterly-annual-office-cleaning-budget-forecast/) predictable.

items.name: Attach the Exact Building Cleaning Exhibit to the Lease
items.text: Never sign a lease referencing "building-standard cleaning" without attaching the full nightly, weekly, monthly, and annual task matrix as an executed exhibit.

items.name: Define Trash Liner, Glass, and Breakroom Boundaries Clearly
items.text: Clarify whether base rent covers kitchenette sink sanitizing, interior conference glass, and private in-suite restrooms, or price those exact line items separately upfront.

items.name: Require LEED / Green Seal GS-37 & HEPA Vacuum Specs
items.text: Insert language mandating Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice chemicals with OSHA HazCom Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and HEPA-filtered vacuums to protect suite air quality.

items.name: Negotiate a Credit or Cure Remedy for Missed Nights
items.text: Include a written 24-hour cure notice and pro-rata rent/OpEx credit if the landlord's contractor repeatedly skips trash pulls or restroom restocking.

faqs.q: Does a full-service gross (FSG) lease cover breakroom and kitchen cleaning?
faqs.a: Usually only partially. Most FSG cleaning exhibits cover emptying breakroom trash and sweeping or damp-mopping open kitchen floors, while excluding sink scrubbing, counter sanitizing, refrigerator fronts, microwave interiors, and dishwashing. Adding full breakroom sanitation typically costs $12 to $25 per visit.

faqs.q: Can we hire our own cleaning company in a full-service gross building?
faqs.a: Often only with landlord consent. Many Class A buildings require tenants to use the building's master janitorial contractor for supplemental services due to security clearance, elevator access, or union rules, though some allow outside vendors if they carry a compliant COI ($1M/$2M General Liability, Additional Insured, Workers' Compensation).

faqs.q: Why does an FSG landlord exclude interior conference room glass from standard cleaning?
faqs.a: Floor-to-ceiling interior glass partitions require specialized streak-free squeegee labor and scratch-free microfiber protocols that slow down nightly routes. Landlords leave interior glass as a tenant add-on ($15 to $35 per visit) unless negotiated into the lease.

faqs.q: What happens to FSG cleaning costs in Year 2 and beyond?
faqs.a: In most US FSG leases, you pay zero direct janitorial escalation during your Base Year, but your lease passes through increases in building-wide cleaning wages, payroll taxes, and supply inflation above the Base Year expense stop—often adjusted via a 95% building occupancy gross-up clause.

faqs.q: Are OSHA HazCom and Bloodborne Pathogens standards the landlord's responsibility in an FSG lease?
faqs.a: For base-building work, the landlord's master contractor must maintain OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200) Safety Data Sheets and OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) protocols. If your company hires a separate supplemental crew for private suite areas, you must verify that vendor's COI and OSHA compliance directly.
